title: Lifting a stably-free complex from a residue quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that every element of $1+I$ is invertible in $R$. Call a module $M$ over a ring $A$ finite stably free if $M\oplus A^{\oplus m}\cong A^{\oplus n}$ for some integers $m,n\ge0$. Let $K$ be an object of $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] that is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], that is, isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules. Let $E^\bullet$ be a bounded-above complex of finite stably free $R/I$-modules representing $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$ in $D(R/I)$. Then $K$ is represented in $D(R)$ by a bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ of finite stably free $R$-modules such that $P^\bullet\otimes_RR/I$ is isomorphic to $E^\bullet$ as a complex; moreover, $P^i$ is free for every $i$ such that $E^i$ is free.

proof.text: Use the class of finite stably free modules. Mathlib makes stably free modules projective. Prove the binary-product class condition by choosing finite free stabilizations: stabilizations of M and N combine to one of M × N; if M and M × N are stably free, rearrange the stabilizations to stabilize N. Transfer finiteness and stable freeness along the given module isomorphism. This is the two-out-of-three property of Tag 0BC4, not closure under arbitrary direct summands.

Apply the finite-module surjectivity-detection lemma to maps of class members. Apply the finite stably free module-lifting theorem separately to each E.X i to supply the term-lifting hypothesis of the general complex-lifting lemma.

Use exactly Classical.choose hK as the representative. Classical.choose_spec hK supplies its bound, finite free terms and derived isomorphism to K. Free modules are stably free, so this is a representative in the chosen class. The given hE is the required derived reduction isomorphism for this same representative. Apply lem-sc-complex-lift-class-projective with these verified hypotheses to obtain P, its bound, class terms, its derived isomorphism to K and a complex isomorphism from its reduction to E.

Evaluate the complex reduction isomorphism at each i and transfer freeness from E.X i to the reduced term of P. Each term of P is finite stably free, hence projective. Apply the finite-projective freeness-detection theorem to this actual P.X i. This proves the free-term clause simultaneously without changing the selected complex.

lean.statement: theorem exists_stablyFree_lift_mod_ideal {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hunits : ∀ x : I, IsUnit (1 + (x : R))) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R ⧸ I))] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) (hK : IsPseudoCoherent K) (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ) (hEbound : ∃ b : ℤ, E.IsStrictlyLE b) (hEterms : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) (E.X i) ∧ Module.IsStablyFree (R ⧸ I) (E.X i)) (hE : Nonempty (Q.obj (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (Classical.choose hK)) ≅ Q.obj E)) : ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ, (∃ b : ℤ, P.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R (P.X i) ∧ Module.IsStablyFree R (P.X i)) ∧ Nonempty (Q.obj P ≅ K) ∧ Nonempty (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ≅ E) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free (R ⧸ I) (E.X i) → Module.Free R (P.X i))
